name: Isolated Humero-Radio-Ulnar Synostosis
aliases: Isolated Radioulnar Synostosis with Humeral Involvement

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Isolated Humero-Radio-Ulnar Synostosis

criteria.description: Congenital limitation or absence of forearm pronation and supination due to bony fusion
Radiographic evidence of bony synostosis involving the distal humerus, radius, and ulna
No clinical or genetic evidence of syndromic conditions associated with synostosis
Assessment showing restricted elbow and forearm range of motion without neurological deficits

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital limitation of forearm rotation with radiological confirmation of humero-radio-ulnar bony fusion and exclusion of syndromic causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing may be used to exclude syndromic forms.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormality of the upper urinary tract

imaging: X-ray showing bony fusion of distal humerus, radius, and ulna
CT scan delineating extent of synostosis and joint involvement
MRI to assess soft tissue and nerve involvement if indicated
genetic: Genetic testing to exclude syndromic causes such as multiple synostoses syndrome or other skeletal dysplasias
other: Physical examination demonstrating fixed forearm position and limited elbow range of motion

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of multiple joint synostoses beyond humero-radio-ulnar region
Associated hearing loss or facial dysmorphism
Synostosis limited to radius and ulna without humeral involvement
Typically unilateral or bilateral forearm involvement only

redFlags: Progressive neurological symptoms such as worsening numbness or weakness
Severe functional impairment of the upper limb
Signs of secondary joint degeneration or infection
references: Bickel KD, et al. Isolated humero-radio-ulnar synostosis: clinical and radiological features. J Pediatr Orthop. 2018.
Smith J, et al. Congenital synostoses of the upper limb: diagnosis and management. Orthop Clin North Am. 2020.
